briefing:
OPENAI PRE-CALL BRIEFING

Note: This is written from my own knowledge, which has a cutoff date. Figures and leadership details may be out of date, so verify anything critical before quoting it on the call.

OVERVIEW
OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company founded in December 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco. It began as a nonprofit and later added a capped-profit arm in 2019. It has since been working to restructure its for-profit entity, a process that drew public scrutiny and legal challenges. Its stated mission is to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits humanity. The company reached mainstream prominence with ChatGPT's launch in November 2022. Headcount has grown into the thousands.

LEADERSHIP
Sam Altman is CEO and a co-founder. Greg Brockman, also a co-founder, serves as president. Altman was briefly ousted by the board in November 2023 and reinstated within days. Several senior figures have departed since, including co-founder Ilya Sutskever (2024) and former CTO Mira Murati (2024). Leadership roles may have shifted since my knowledge ends, so check the current org chart.

FUNDING AND FINANCIALS
Microsoft has been the largest strategic backer, committing roughly 13 billion dollars in total. A 2024 round raised about 6.6 billion dollars at a valuation near 157 billion dollars, with later reports of valuations well above that. Revenue was reported at around 3.7 billion dollars for 2024, with projections to grow substantially, though the company has also reported heavy losses driven by compute costs. Treat all numbers as approximate.

PRODUCTS
ChatGPT is the flagship, offered in free, Plus, Pro, Team, and Enterprise tiers. The API provides access to models such as the GPT-4 family and reasoning models in the o-series. Other offerings include DALL-E for images, Sora for video, Whisper for speech, and Codex-style coding tools. Enterprise customers care most about security, data privacy, and admin controls.

RECENT NEWS
Themes include the push to convert to a standard for-profit structure, intense competition from Anthropic, Google, and Meta, large infrastructure commitments such as the Stargate data center initiative, and ongoing copyright litigation, including the New York Times suit. Confirm the latest developments before the call.
